text:
Jin Park: thinking out loud — proposing a small 'materializer' layer that sits between WeightSource and the runtime. it would accept a MaterializeRequest and handle hybrid checkpoints (safetensors, tar.gz bundles, legacy npz). reasons: unify streaming vs index-first, centralize checksums/telemetry, and surface partial materialization APIs.
Sara Li: +1 for a single abstraction. question: how does it expose errors? streaming formats can fail mid-read. do we bubble IO errors up or return a partial manifest and let caller decide?
Mike O'Neill: I'd rather we return a deterministic contract: either full MaterializedHandle or a RetryableStream object plus a set of guarantees. callers get explicit states: COMPLETE | PARTIAL_STREAM | FAILED. avoids surprise exceptions in hot paths.
Alex Gomez: we should avoid forcing the runtime to understand format details. Materializer -> provides hooks: `open_stream(kv)` and `provide_index()`; runtime picks which to call. keep the fallback policy policy-driven, not hard-coded.
Priya Shah: ops perspective: rollout must allow us to toggle index-first fallback off for a tenant. can this be a per-namespace flag in the MaterializeRequest? we need telemetry that counts when fallbacks happen and byte-cost of re-materializations.
Jin Park: implementation sketch: MaterializeRequest = {model_id, shard_id, preferred_mode:[STREAM_FIRST|INDEX_FIRST], namespace_flags, trace_id}. Materializer returns a JSON-like manifest plus either a streaming URL or a memory-backed mapping. also emits `materialize.event` telemetry.
Sara Li: tradeoffs: STREAM_FIRST is lower tail-latency on cold start but complicates eviction (we may have half-initialized layers). INDEX_FIRST guarantees locality and easier OOM accounting. need a clear eviction contract for PARTIAL_STREAM.
Mike O'Neill: for PARTIAL_STREAM handle we should expose `pin(range)` so runtime can ensure critical layers are materialized synchronously. pin failures are explicit. that lets higher layers request hot-start of attention/query kernels.
Alex Gomez: runtime changes: small — call Materializer.materialize(request), if PARTIAL_STREAM then attempt pin for first N layers; if pin fails, trigger graceful degrade: route to smaller quantized variant if configured. fallback policies remain in routing layer.
Priya Shah: ops: suggest adding a `materializer.health` metric and a `materializer.fallback_rate{namespace}`. and a `materializer.repair_job` that can reconcile partially materialized shards overnight to flatten long-tail cost spikes.
warmup-bot: deploy note: canary of materializer-v1 scheduled to eng-ml-canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC. watch `materialize.latency` and `materialize.fallback_rate`.
Jin Park: next steps: I'll draft an RFC with API signatures and the error/state enum. wants volunteers for review: @Sara Li, @Alex Gomez, @Mike O'Neill, @Priya Shah — can you chime in on eviction and telemetry sections?
Sara Li: happy to take eviction section.
Alex Gomez: I'll add runtime integration notes and minimal shim examples.
Mike O'Neill: will prototype `pin(range)` semantics in loader.
Priya Shah: I'll draft ops runbook bits and metric names.
Jin Park: thanks — will open RFC this afternoon. short followup: does anyone object to `MaterializeRequest.preferred_mode` being advisory (not enforced)? if not, I'll mark it advisory in the RFC.
Mike O'Neill: ok with advisory. we need strict semantics in the enum docs though.
Sara Li: fine. one more: add an escape hatch `force_index=true` for debugging.
Jin Park: noted. thanks everyone.
